# Plan Example: `/assign` Makes Pydantic Values, Filled From Any URL

A plan as sent before building (2026-11-17), for delulu-smash's `/assign`. Worth noting as an example: it
opens by naming the existing rules it reverses (in `spec/`), before anything else, and its edge cases include
the case the user cared about most and that it can't handle (JavaScript-built pages). Then it was **revised
after throwaway tests** (bottom section): the tests overturned the first design (a code-only browser step
couldn't get the data) and produced a better one (the AI writes a parser instead of copying values). Not
built when saved; the decisions at the end are still open.

---

**Rules this reverses**, both in `spec/services/ui/variables.md` ("/assign", "Structured values only"):

1. "…or a polars DataFrame": `/assign` would **no longer make DataFrames**.
2. "Several records are a DataFrame, never a list of records": a list of records would **become the way** to
   hold several rows.

`r1` from the agent's tools and `q1` from SmashDb consoles stay DataFrames. Only what `/assign` makes changes.

## Plan: `/assign` makes pydantic values, and can fill them from any URL

### What you'd see

```
/assign mac_aerials = Little Mac's aerials from https://ultimateframedata.com/little_mac

┌ proposal (from a web page: filled by AI, not checked) ─────────────────────────┐
│ class Aerial(BaseModel, frozen=True):                                           │
│     move: str                    # "Nair"                                       │
│     startup_frame: int           # first active frame                           │
│     base_damage: float           # as listed (no 1v1 1.2x)                      │
│     landing_lag: int                                                            │
│                                                                                 │
│ mac_aerials = from_url("https://ultimateframedata.com/little_mac", list[Aerial])│
└ Enter runs · Esc drops ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Enter → mac_aerials: list[Aerial], 5 items  (page: 41 KB → 9,800 tokens, 1 AI call, $0.002)
        Aerial(move='Nair', startup_frame=4, base_damage=6.0, landing_lag=6), …
```

You can edit the class before pressing Enter (rename a field, drop one, add `notes: str | None`), and it
fills whatever class is there when it runs. That's the demo pattern: you define a pydantic class, and the AI
fills it.

Without a URL, it works as today, but makes models instead of DataFrames:

```
/assign top5 = the five best players in q1
→ class PlayerWins(BaseModel, frozen=True): player: str; wins: int
  top5 = [PlayerWins(**row) for row in q1.sort("wins", descending=True).head(5).iter_rows(named=True)]
```

### Interfaces

```python
# pkgs/ds/ai/extract.py (new, generic: usable from /assign, cells and scripts)
def page_text(url: str, max_tokens: int = 15_000) -> PageText: ...
    # ds.util.http GET (logged); JSON / CSV as is; HTML -> drop script/style/nav (bs4) -> Markdown (markdownify,
    #   which keeps <table>s as Markdown tables); cut at max_tokens and say so
@dataclass
class PageText:
    url: str; text: str; kind: Literal["html", "json", "csv", "text"]; truncated: bool

def from_url[T](url: str, shape: type[T]) -> T: ...
    # page_text(url) -> one AI call with output_type=shape: "fill only from this page; never invent a value;
    #   a field the page doesn't have is None if optional, else fail" -> the validated value
    #   raises NotOnPage("...why...") when the page doesn't hold it (eg drawn by JavaScript)

# services/ui/ui/assign.py (changed)
value_problem(value) -> str: ...
    # allowed: basic | list[basic] | Model | list[Model] (one class); a Model's fields: basic, list[basic],
    #   Model, list[Model], or None; refused now: pl.DataFrame, dict, tuple, set
run(session, code) -> Ran: ...      # as today; the namespace also gets `from_url`
Assign.basis: Literal["computed", "knowledge", "extracted"]   # new: "from a web page: filled by AI, not checked"
```

### Workflows

```python
# /assign with a URL
propose(session, token, "mac_aerials = Little Mac's aerials from https://…")
  -> Assign(name="mac_aerials", code="class Aerial…\nmac_aerials = from_url(url, list[Aerial])", basis="extracted")
# user presses Enter
run(session, code)
  exec(code)                         # defines Aerial, calls from_url
    from_url(url, list[Aerial])
      page_text(url) -> PageText(kind="html", text=<Markdown with the frame tables>, truncated=False)
      extract_agent.run(text, output_type=list[Aerial]) -> [Aerial(...), ...]   # validated by pydantic
  value_problem(value) -> ""         # list of one model: allowed
  bind mac_aerials (and the Aerial class)

# later, your own conversion
to_df(mac_aerials) -> pl.DataFrame   # not part of this plan
```

### When something goes wrong

| Case | What you see under the code |
|---|---|
| The page builds its data with JavaScript (Google Finance's history) | `NotOnPage: the page's HTML has no daily prices; it's probably drawn by JavaScript`. Nothing is bound. |
| The page doesn't have a field (e.g. no `landing_lag`) | a required field fails: "landing_lag isn't on the page; make it `int \| None` or drop it". An optional one is `None`. |
| A huge page | cut at 15,000 tokens; the result line says "page truncated", so a short list doesn't look complete |
| 403, bot check, login | the status and the site, from the request log; nothing is bound |
| The AI makes up a value | the main risk. Mitigated by the "only from this page" rule and the `extracted` label; spot-check it, as with a `knowledge` literal |
| Code still makes a DataFrame | "Not assigned: /assign makes models, not DataFrames; use `[Model(**row) for row in df.iter_rows(named=True)]`" |

### Your decisions

1. **Drop DataFrames from `/assign`** (reverses the spec rule above). **Recommend yes**: models in, `to_df`
   later. The tools' `r1` and consoles' `q1` stay DataFrames.
2. **Lists of records and nested models:** allow `list[Model]` at the top and `Model` / `list[Model]` inside
   fields (this reverses "never a list of records"). **Recommend yes**: it's how a page's table becomes rows
   without a DataFrame.
3. **Where `from_url` lives:** **recommend `pkgs/ds/ai/extract.py`**, so cells, scripts and later the chat
   agent can use it, not only `/assign`.
4. **Page cap:** **recommend 15,000 tokens** (about 60 KB of text, around $0.002 per extraction with Haiku),
   to keep each call cheap and bounded.
5. **JavaScript pages:** **recommend failing clearly for now** (`NotOnPage`), and adding a browser later if
   you hit pages you care about.

## Follow-up question: "so this will just not work for JavaScript-built pages?"

Right, not as planned. `from_url` downloads the HTML; Google Finance sends only the current snapshot, and its
history arrives later when the page's JavaScript asks for it. What would make it work, most to least reliable:

| Option | How | Google Finance |
|---|---|---|
| A data API for that site's kind of data | a real source | ✅ exact |
| Capture the page's own data requests, with a browser: `page_text(url, render=True)` | headless Chromium, record the JSON requests the page makes, give that JSON to the AI | ⚠️ probably; Google may block automated browsers, and the JSON is undocumented |
| Rendered text, with a browser | open the page, wait for JavaScript, read its text | ❌ mostly; the chart is drawn as a picture |

The browser mode is an add-on to `page_text` only: `from_url`, the classes and `/assign` stay the same.

## Revised after three tests (2026-11-17)

Throwaway scripts in `/tmp` (deleted after), against Google Finance's AAPL page, on Haiku 5.5 via the Gateway,
capped at 15 model requests each.

### What the tests found

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Code-only browser: load, wait, capture the page's JSON | ❌ ~40 responses, no price history. The biggest "numbers" response was SVG drawings, not data. |
| Code-only browser, then click "1Y" | ✅ the page's own request (`rpcids=c2u4wc`, 26 KB) held 252 days: date, close, volume. Google didn't block headless Chromium. |
| Harness `PlaywrightBrowser` agent, in-page JS recorder | ❌ clicked 1Y but the recorder missed the response (Google keeps its own reference to the request functions). Honest `NotOnPage`, no invented values. 38 s, $0.028. |
| Harness agent clicks; **our code** records bodies; **AI copies** the rows | ✅ 251 of 252 rows (the model dropped one). 50 s, $0.024, ~12k output tokens. |
| Same, but the **AI writes a parser**, tests it with `try_parse`, our code runs it | ✅ 251 rows (a repeated date skipped on purpose); all 249 rows the independent check could find match exactly; the AI's 3 sample rows all present. 40 s, $0.034. |

Also learned:
- The harness launches Playwright's own Chromium, or attaches to a running one through `cdp_url`. Our system
  `/usr/bin/chromium` (on every Omarchy machine) works through `cdp_url`: no download.
- `network_requests` lists URLs, not bodies, so the harness alone can't get POST-loaded data; our recorder
  has to sit on the harness's page (reached in the test through a `for_run` subclass and the private
  `_session.page`: fragile across harness updates, so a test must pin it).
- Numbers in a response aren't proof of data (the SVG trap): the agent picks responses by dated values.

### Revised design

```python
# pkgs/ds/ai/extract.py
def page_text(url: str, max_tokens: int = 15_000) -> PageText: ...   # quick path, unchanged

def from_url[T](url: str, shape: type[T]) -> FromUrl[T]: ...
    # 1. quick: page_text(url) -> one AI call (copy) -> value, or NotOnPage
    # 2. fallback on NotOnPage: _browse(url, shape)

async def _browse(url: str, shape: type[T]) -> Recipe | Copied[T] | NotOnPage: ...
    # system_chromium() -> cdp_url  (/usr/bin/chromium --headless --remote-debugging-port, stopped after)
    # agent = Agent(output_type=[Recipe, Copied[shape], NotOnPage],
    #               capabilities=[RecordingBrowser(cdp_url=..., allowed_domains=[host_of(url)])],
    #               tools=[start_recording, data_responses, read_response, try_parse])
    # usage_limits: 15 requests

class Recipe(BaseModel):            # regular data (series, big tables): the AI writes how to read it
    steps: list[str]                #   what it did on the page, eg ["click 1Y"]
    response: str                   #   which recorded response, eg "rpcids=c2u4wc"
    parse_code: str                 #   def parse(body: str) -> list[Shape]
    sample: list[Any]               #   3 rows read by eye: checked against the parser's rows
class Copied[T](BaseModel):         # small or irregular data: the AI copies the values (as the quick path)
    value: T

@dataclass
class FromUrl[T]:
    value: T; how: Literal["copied", "parsed"]; parse_code: str = ""; steps: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
```

```python
# /assign aapl_daily = daily closes for the past year from <google finance url>
from_url(url, list[DailyClose])
  quick:    page_text -> snapshot only -> NotOnPage
  fallback: navigate -> start_recording -> snapshot -> click 1Y -> data_responses -> read_response
            -> try_parse ×3 -> Recipe(steps=["click 1Y"], response="rpcids=c2u4wc", parse_code=..., sample=[...])
  our code: run parse_code on the full body -> 251 rows; sample rows present? -> value
  proposal shows the parser, so the user reads it and can re-run it without the AI
```

### Edges added

| Case | What you see |
|---|---|
| The parser's rows don't include the AI's sample rows | "the parser doesn't match what the page shows"; nothing bound |
| The parser raises on the full body | its traceback under the code; nothing bound |
| The page changes its format later | a re-run's parser fails loudly, not wrong rows |
| More than 15 model requests | stops; `NotOnPage("gave up after 15 steps")` |
| A harness update moves the private page attribute | caught by a test that pins it |
| A system Chromium update stops working with the `playwright` package (versions drift: Omarchy updates Chromium, Playwright expects its own) | the fallback fails with the connection error, not wrong data. Fix: update `playwright`, or let the harness download its own (`auto_install_chromium=True`, ~130 MB per machine) |

### Decisions (updated)

1-5 as above, plus:
6. **Fallback = harness `PlaywrightBrowser` agent + our recorder.** **Recommend yes** (tested).
7. **Recipe for regular data, copy for small or irregular.** **Recommend yes**: exact and re-runnable.
8. **System Chromium through `cdp_url`**, no download. **Recommend yes** (tested).
9. **Running AI-written parse code**: in `/assign` it's shown in the proposal and runs when the user
   presses Enter, as all `/assign` code does. **Recommend yes**, no auto-run.

## Built (2026-11-17): what changed from the plan

Built without Replay, parsers restricted and auto-run (the user's choice), everything the AI ran shown.

| Change from the plan | Why |
|---|---|
| `from_url(url, shape, what)`: a third argument saying what to get | the shape alone can't say "past year": a run clicked 1M and returned 21 rows |
| `from_url` returns the plain value; what it did is a separate report (shown as a folded chat row) | `x = from_url(...)` should be the list itself |
| Parsers get stand-ins for `json` / `re` / `datetime` / `math`, not the modules | the real modules reach others through attributes (`json.codecs.open`, `re.enum.sys`): found in review |
| A failing recipe is sent back to the AI (up to 3 times) instead of failing the run | the AI's final answer sometimes differed from the parser it had tested |
| The recipe's sample rows are typed as the item class | an untyped sample came back as empty rows, rejecting correct parsers (a bug in the first build) |
| The recorder waits for data still arriving before listing it | a click's data comes back after the click returns: one run saw nothing |
| Page text keeps values' CSS-class labels (`landinglag: 16`) | ultimateframedata labels numbers only by class: the AI mixed up landing lag and shield advantage |
| The quick path refuses local and private addresses | the browser path already did |

Measured on the built version: Little Mac aerials (page text) 5 s, $0.001, values correct after the label
fix; AAPL past year (browser) 31 s, $0.026, 251 rows. Runs vary: of the Google Finance runs while building,
several failed for the reasons above, and the AI still decides what to click.
